title: Cat-in-Yard Intrusion by Hour
dataSources: Bird acoustic detections (`birdnet:detection`), wildlife-camera visits (`wildlifecam:visit`), nest-box state (`nestbox:event`), frog-call activity (`frogcall:detection`), and pollinator counts (`pollinator:count`).
app: Wildlife telemetry from BirdNET, trail and feeder cameras, nest-box sensors, frog-call detectors, and pollinator counters streamed to Splunk HEC via MQTT, APIs, and scripted imports.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=wildlifecam:visit species="cat"
| eval hour=strftime(_time,"%H")
| stats count as visits by hour
| sort hour
description: Counts neighborhood cat visits by hour so you can understand predation pressure on feeders and nests.
value: Domestic-cat traffic is often a bigger birding factor than expected, and hourly patterns help target deterrents better.
implementation: Label cat detections from trail or garden cameras and aggregate them by hour of day.
visualization: Histogram of cat visits by hour.
grandmaExplanation: It maps when cats are most often coming into the yard where wildlife uses the space.
